newsitem.title: UK: Physical aluminium sees weaker tone in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Physical aluminium sees weaker tone in Europe.

text.p: Physical aluminium premiums had a slightly softer tone in Europe after more material found its way onto the market, but have the potential to tighten, traders said.
At least one major aluminium player was thought to have released some of its financed stocks, increasing availability, they added.
"They are opening the door a bit," one trader said.
A cash/threes contango which narrowed to about $10 two weeks ago reduced returns from financing operations, but on Wednesday the spread was indicated at $25/$24. The normal level is about $35.

There were no major moves in premiums but Russian off-grade A0 metal in Rotterdam was $5 weaker at $5/$15 over LME cash and Western duty unpaid material in Rotterdam was down by a like amount around $50/$55.
Some traders said lower futures prices had drawn out more business. "Even Germany is starting to buy, which is quite incredible," one said.
But others said the strong dollar had cancelled out the more attractive LME price in much of Europe and the summer lull had already set in.
Several major physical longs and shorts were lurking in the market and if they fail to match up, the market could see some movement, a source in continental Europe said.
"If big people have to start covering, premiums can go higher, but I don't see them going to the sky," he said.
The future direction of premiums were linked to the cash/threes contango, with a tightening back to around $10 seeing premiums weaker, traders said.
Easier premiums in the U.S. Midwest were influencing the market, dealers said.
